# Overview / TLDR 

Recall that Task 4 is the task where we ask the participant to find the highest sloped on the CDF (i.e., find mode on CDF). Aka `MaxSlope` Operator. 

We ran the following models: 

- The [Exponential model](@sec-exponential)
- The [Lomax model](@sec-lomax)
- **best-performing model**^[... by LOO model comparison] The [Weibull model](@sec-weibull)
- The [Log-Normal model](@sec-logNormal)

Finally we compared all models in [here](@sec-model-compare). 

# Set up

Read in data and relevant scales: 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true"}
task_df <- read_rds(here("data", "part1", "task.rds"))
participants <- read_rds(here("data", "part1", "participants.rds"))
exp1_x <- make_va_scale(data_min = -5, data_max = 5, px_min = 50, px_max = 585)
exp1_y <- make_va_scale(data_min = 0, data_max = 1, px_min = 410, px_max = 15)
```
:::


Ratio related helper function: 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# x: one unit in data maps to (585 - 50)/(5 - (-5)) in pixel
# y: one unit in data maps to (410 - 15)/(1 - 0) in pixel
data_to_screen_slope <- function(k) {
  return(k * 395 / 53.5)
}
data_to_va_slope <- function(data_x, data_y, dist, px_per_mm) {
  eps <- 1e-6
  s_y <- abs(
    exp1_y$data_to_va(data_y + eps, dist, px_per_mm) -
      exp1_y$data_to_va(data_y, dist, px_per_mm)
  ) /
    eps
  s_x <- (abs(
    exp1_x$data_to_va(data_x + eps, dist, px_per_mm) -
      exp1_x$data_to_va(data_x, dist, px_per_mm)
  ) /
    eps)
  return(s_y / s_x)
}
```
:::


Get task-related specific data: 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
task4_df <- task_df %>%
  filter(task == "task4") %>%
  select(-slider.x, -slider.y) %>%
  right_join(participants, by = join_by(participantId)) %>%
  mutate(
    data.resp.slope = dsgt(
      data.select.x,
      param.mu,
      param.sigma,
      param.lambda,
      param.p,
      param.q,
      mean.cent = FALSE
    ),
    data.ans.slope = dsgt(
      param.mu,
      param.mu,
      param.sigma,
      param.lambda,
      param.p,
      param.q,
      mean.cent = FALSE
    ),
    data.ans.x = param.mu,
    data.ans.y = 0.5 *
      (psgt(
        data.ans.x + tolerance,
        param.mu,
        param.sigma,
        param.lambda,
        param.p,
        param.q,
        mean.cent = FALSE
      ) +
        psgt(
          data.ans.x - tolerance,
          param.mu,
          param.sigma,
          param.lambda,
          param.p,
          param.q,
          mean.cent = FALSE
        )),
    va.resp.slope = data.resp.slope *
      data_to_va_slope(
        data.select.x,
        data.select.y,
        dist_to_screen,
        pixelToMM
      ),
    va.ans.slope = data.ans.slope *
      data_to_va_slope(
        data.ans.x,
        data.ans.y,
        dist_to_screen,
        pixelToMM
      )
  )
```

# Exponential Model {#sec-exponential}

Math model: 

$$
\begin{align*}
\texttt{error\_i} &\sim \text{Exponential}(\lambda_{\text{PID}[i]}) \\ 
\log(\lambda_j) &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\lambda, \sigma_\lambda) \\ 
\mu_\lambda &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \\ 
\sigma_\lambda &\sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 1) 
\end{align*}
$$

Formula and prior: 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
f <- bf(error ~ 0, mu ~ (1 | participantId), family = exponential())

# mu has log-link, so we don't pose any bounds on it
p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, lb = 0)
)
```
:::



::: {.cell}

:::


Fit the model: 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
model.exponential <- task4_df %>%
  mutate(error = abs(va.resp.slope - va.ans.slope)) %>%
  # brms need rsp > 0 for exp
  mutate(error = ifelse(error < tolerance, tolerance, error)) %>%
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    prior = p,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task4.exponential"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    iter = 6000
  )
```
:::


# Lomax Model {#sec-lomax}

Lomax is Pareto Type II distribution. 

Math model: 

$$
\begin{align*}\text{error}_i &\sim \text{Lomax}(\lambda_{\text{PID}[i]}, \alpha_{\text{PID}[i]}) \\ 
\log(\lambda_j) &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_\lambda, \sigma_\lambda^2) \\ 
\log(\alpha_j) &\sim \text{Normal}(\mu_\alpha, \sigma_\alpha^2) \\ 
\mu_\lambda, \mu_\alpha &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \\ 
\sigma_\lambda, \sigma_\alpha &\sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 1)
\end{align*}
$$


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# define the lomax family
lomax_family <- custom_family(
  "lomax",
  dpars = c("mu", "lambda", "alpha"), # includes mu as required
  links = c("identity", "log", "log"), # appropriate links
  lb = c(-Inf, 0, 0), # appropriate bounds
  type = "real"
)

stan_funs <- "
  real lomax_lpdf(real y, real mu, real lambda, real alpha) {
    return pareto_type_2_lpdf(y | 0, lambda, alpha);  
  }

  real lomax_rng(real mu, real lambda, real alpha) {
    return pareto_type_2_rng(0, lambda, alpha);  
  }
"
```
:::


Specify formula and prior: 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Define the formula for the model
f <- bf(
  error ~ 0,
  mu ~ 0,
  alpha ~ (1 | participantId),
  lambda ~ (1 | participantId)
)

p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = alpha),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = alpha, lb = 0),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = lambda),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = lambda, lb = 0)
)
```
:::



::: {.cell}

:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
model.lomax <- task4_df %>%
  mutate(error = abs(va.resp.slope - va.ans.slope)) %>%
  mutate(error = ifelse(error < tolerance, tolerance, error)) %>%
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    family = lomax_family,
    prior = p,
    stanvars = stanvar(scode = stan_funs, block = "functions"),
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task4.lomax"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
    iter = 6000,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE)
  )
```

```{.r .cell-code}

posterior_predict_lomax <- function(i, draws, ...) {
  alpha <- draws$dpars$alpha[i]
  lambda <- draws$dpars$lambda[i]
  # Use Stan's rng function indirectly via brms
  lomax_rng(0, lambda, alpha)
}

log_lik_lomax <- function(i, prep) {
  alpha <- brms::get_dpar(prep, "alpha", i = i)
  lambda <- brms::get_dpar(prep, "lambda", i = i)
  y <- prep$data$Y[i]
  lomax_lpdf(y, 0, lambda, alpha)
}
```

# Weibull distribution {#sec-weibull}

- [wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weibull_distribution)
- [stan](https://mc-stan.org/docs/functions-reference/positive_continuous_distributions.html#weibull-distribution)
- it's also implemented in brms! So unlike the [Lomax model](@sec-lomax), we don't need to write custom functions. 

Math model: 

$$
\begin{align}
\texttt{error}_i &\sim \text{Weibull}(\mu_{\text{PID}[i]}, k_{\text{PID}[i]}) \\
\log(\mu_j) &= \alpha_j \\ 
\log(k_j) &= \beta_j \\ 
\alpha_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\alpha, \sigma_\alpha) \\ 
\beta_j &\sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\beta, \sigma_\beta) \\ 
\mu_\alpha, \mu_\beta &\sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1) \\ 
\sigma_\alpha, \sigma_beta &\sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 1)
\end{align}
$$

Specify formula and prior: 


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
f <- bf(
  error ~ 0,
  mu ~ (1 | participantId), # log link
  shape ~ (1 | participantId), # log link
  family = weibull
)

p <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, lb = 0),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept, dpar = shape),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = sd, group = participantId, dpar = shape, lb = 0)
)
```
:::



::: {.cell}

:::


Fit the model:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
model.weibull <- task4_df %>%
  mutate(error = abs(va.resp.slope - va.ans.slope)) %>%
  mutate(error = ifelse(error < tolerance, tolerance, error)) %>% # brms needs value to be > 0
  brm(
    formula = f,
    data = .,
    prior = p,
    chains = 4,
    cores = 4,
    file = here("analysis", "fitted_models", "part1", "task4.weibull"),
    file_refit = "on_change",
    save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
    iter = 6000,
    adapt_delta = 0.95,
  )
```
